The Giant Rock (Japanese: 巨石 ) is a powerful material in . It is an ancient, giant rock that contains massive amounts of Primal energy. It was later used by Lysandre to create a -like construct under his control

==History==
===Pokémon the Series===
====Pre-series====
In the ancient times in the Hoenn region, Primal and Primal clashed, expanding the land and seas as they tried to take possession of the incredible source of power that is the Giant Rock.

At some point after that, ancient people discovered the Giant Rock and hid it away under a temple atop a mountain. Said temple being only found through the use of two Key Stones.

==== ====
In the Mega Evolution Special II, Alain, Mairin, , and Lysandre were looking for the giant rock in ruins and thanks to the latters's Key Stones, they found the rock within ruins atop a mountain. As Lysandre's scientists started researching on it, Mega Rayquaza appeared and tried to attack them. Alain and Steven attempted to fend off the , but the Giant Rock disappeared. In the Mega Evolution Special III, the super-ancient Pokémon battled over the Giant Rock, due to being attracted to its massive amount of Primal energy. While Alain and Steven fought off Groudon and Kyogre, Lysandre managed to secure the giant stone by blinding out Rayquaza. During the events of Mega Evolution Special IV, Chespie got hurt while saving Squishy from Team Flare, causing the to absorb the energy around it and enter a comatose state.
 
After this, the Giant Rock made a brief appearance in Unlocking Some Respect!, where it was seen in Xerosic's lab. In Rocking Kalos Defenses!, it was revealed that, in case Team Flare lost control of the two Zygarde, Lysandre had planned for it to absorb Chespie and transform into a copy of Zygarde, which would then collide with Anistar City's Sundial and release enough energy to wipe out all life on the . It was created when , Mairin, and invaded Lysandre Labs, destroying the laboratory during its conception and forcing all Team Flare agents present to flee. It could not be stopped by Ash, Alain, Steven, Professor Sycamore, Serena and their strongest Pokémon, although Ash-Greninja was able to sense Chespie's presence in the giant creature and marked its location with a .

In Forming a More Perfect Union!, the was helped by Kalos Gym Leaders, Diantha, Meyer, and Malva. Together, they all helped clear or destroy some of the Giant Rock's roots in order to pave the way for Ash, Alain and their Pokémon to enter the Giant Rock's inner core and rescue Chespie, which deprived the Giant Rock of its power source, thus rendering it inert. Lysandre ultimately had to personally power it back up using his control device, but in response Squishy and Z2 transformed into Zygarde, which was able to match the Giant Rock in combat. Although Lysandre attempted to fight back, he was defeated when Ash's Greninja, Pikachu and Alain's Charizard destroyed his control device, allowing Zygarde to attack the Giant Rock with , which made a massive hole in it. It was finally destroyed by Squishy and Z2's , of which Lysandre was engulfed in the explosion and leaving his final fate unclear. It also appeared in Till We Compete Again!, during a video fantasy and a flashback.

==Characteristics==
In its Zygarde form, the Giant Rock has roughly the same body shape as 's , except it is much larger. Its upper body is primarily made out of stone, with a glowing red crystal serving as its "eye", whereas its lower body is composed out of vines. These vines also serve as a defense mechanism to protect the core body from attacks.

The Giant Rock is partly hollow inside, with its "innards" being composed out of glowing red crystals, with Chespie, its power source, at the center. These red crystals will likewise grow and shift to serve as a defense mechanism for its energy source. Even after the power source is removed, Lysandre still managed to power it up remotely using a control device coupled to his gauntlet.

Due to its vast size and mindless nature, the Giant Rock is extremely difficult to slow down, let alone defeat. In order to stop it, , Diantha, , Alain, Meyer, Malva, and , as well as eight Kalos Gym Leaders, needed to have all their strongest Pokémon team up against it. Even then, after Lysandre powered it up again, Squishy and Z2 had to transform into Zygarde Complete Forme to stop it, and only managed to do so after Ash's Pikachu, , and Alain's Charizard destroyed Lysandre's control device.

==Trivia==
As a Zygarde, the Giant Rock's characteristics parallel those of the Meta Groudon from Jirachi: Wish Maker. Both of them are artificial, corrupted, bigger versions of a Legendary Pokémon, created by characters associating with villainous teams whose goals were to capture and control the real version. Both creatures are also mindless beasts whose sole intentions are to absorb more power.
The Giant Rock in its Zygarde form has a number of similarities with the ultimate weapon. Both are weapons powered by the energy of Pokémon channeled through special stones, are capable of firing catastrophically powerful laser beams, and are used by Lysandre in his bid to destroy and remake the world according to Team Flare's ideals only to have their power sources removed and ultimately be destroyed with Lysandre within them.
It also shares similarities with the Meteonite, being a mysterious rock that can store and unleash energy that is sought for usage as a weapon by one or more villainous teams operating in the region.
It also shares similarities with the -shaped lava creature featured in Pokémon: The Arceus Chronicles. Both are created by an existing item — the original form of the Giant Rock and a Flame Plate, respectively — merging with the power of a Legendary Pokémon through the actions of a villainous team. They then transform into an autonomous weapon in the shape of the legendary Pokémon whose power they fused with, and travel toward a fixed destination that will cause an apocalyptic explosion if they reach it. Both are only stopped through the intervention of a group that includes at least one , and near the end of the battle to stop them, and some of enter the weapon's structure to remove the Pokémon providing its power from within.
It also resembles Ange from . Both are artificial constructs that absorb a Pokémon and take on aspects of its physical appearance, are capable of unleashing giant roots and firing powerful lasers, and are both ultimately destroyed by Zygarde.
